object_description: compact western ensemble with a dominant school volume and sunken gymnasium
design_condition: The compact buildings are concentrated on the west to place the football field farther west and integrate the lawn into the terrain, while stairs, squares and planted edges organize connections to the surrounding district.

positive.statement: The compact western disposition optimizes the placement of the football field in relation to the topography.

position.rationale: The dominant mass is visibly concentrated on the western side of the model.

positive.statement: The new school building establishes a clear volumetric focus and strengthens the connection to the district.

position.rationale: A tall western volume clearly provides the ensemble’s volumetric focus.

positive.statement: The topographical conditions generate differentiated outdoor spaces and organize access to the different user groups.

position.rationale: Open areas and edges around the concentrated masses suggest differentiated outdoor zones.

positive.statement: The address square provides an arrival point that can also accommodate events.

position.rationale: A lower southern approach zone is the most plausible arrival square.

positive.statement: The compact organization supports the educational concept of the small school within the larger school.

position.rationale: The dominant volume’s repeated stacked bands support an internal smaller-school grouping approximation.

positive.statement: The separate gymnasium and auditorium arrangement provides independence for larger events, clubs and neighbourhood use.

position.rationale: A distinct smaller eastern volume is clearly separated from the dominant western school.

positive.statement: The facade design makes a high-quality impression and conveys a certain openness.

position.rationale: Large repeated facade bands and openings are visible on the main school elevations.

negative.statement: The compact urban-planning strategy leaves the surrounding open spaces limited and lacking spatial and atmospheric power.

position.rationale: The compact footprint leaves visibly limited interstitial space around the buildings.

negative.statement: The prominent outside-stair transitions are neither adequate nor practical for people with disabilities.

position.rationale: A southern access edge is approximated, but exterior stairs are not distinctly resolved.

negative.statement: The access areas are generously sized but uninspiring, functioning more as corridors than lounges.

position.rationale: Interior access zones are approximated within the tall school volume.

negative.statement: The childcare rooms are only vertically connected through the general staircase, restricting flexibility of use.

position.rationale: Childcare rooms are approximated inside the main volume; their vertical connection is not visible.

negative.statement: The potential for networking public uses with the outdoor space and district is not exploited.

position.target: public uses and outdoor space connection
position.rationale: The central gap between school and eastern volume is the likely public-outdoor interface.

negative.statement: The gymnasium entrance is difficult to read because of its lateral placement beneath the massive school volume and the adjacent outside staircase.

position.rationale: The eastern volume’s southern-lateral edge provides a constrained entrance location.

negative.statement: The overall appearance is not considered adequate for a primary school in relation to the impressive size of the new building.

position.rationale: The tall dominant school mass is clearly visible and supports the scale and identity critique.
